note: v1 (FIRST DRAFT): ALL OF IT FALLS (jet and horizon, the release). 176 bars (~305 s): 150 bpm held flat from the t7 seam, then a 150 -> 90 decelerando over the horizon. LENS (1-16): E4's lights (strings) catch the fall. THE STRETTO (17-96): the elements enter in turn, each on its OWN cycle - E1 on the chip pulse (5 beats, from 17), E2 'seven' on a pluck (7 sixteenths, from 29), E3 t3's progression on a dark pad (2+2+3, from 41), E5 'the inner orbit' on marimba (3 beats, from 53), the D pedal on the triangle bass in E2's rhythm (from 33), noise hats in 3s from 65 - and every one starts at the phase that lands a cycle exactly on bar 97's downbeat (beat 384): until then they rub, minor and out of phase (E2's F, E3's Eb, E5's G# against the D pedal). THE JET (97): every cycle lands together, the material turns major (F -> F#, Eb -> E), the band locks into a half-time 4/4 (machine kit, triangle bass, a sine sub), E1 re-barred into the bar, E5 and E2 still in 3 and 7 now consonant, and the voice - a CHOIR (a bright, smaller-tract lead with a fifth above and an octave below, a different character from t4's warm soloist) - sings full lines: 'all of it falls into light' (E1 augmented, then E8, E F# D, landed ONCE, on 'light'), 'round and round and then out, then home' (E5), 'we were the far side' (E1 inverted), 'and it was ours' (E2 in the major). A breakdown (121-128) brings the lens back - lights, sub and choir - and the jet returns (129-140). THE HORIZON (141-176): a held D (detuned saws and the sung 'ah', its sub beneath) sinks 5 semitones and closes its filter as the tempo slows: the light redshifting away. First render 72.2 / 72.9 (structure 53, recurrence 19, sub -23 dB): the breakdown, the second jet and a sine sub took it to 87.38 / 87.82 (structure 88, recurrence 49, spectrum 79-82). Levels -11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29. E6 (provisional) and E7 (not posted) join the stretto later. NOT verified by ear.
next: t4 next; then t8: E6/E7 into the stretto, the choir's harmony (diatonic thirds rather than fifths?), the jet's impact.

note: v2 (ROUND TYPE whole): THE STRETTO COMPLETE - t8 now holds E1-E7, as the brief asks. E6 'the tide' (t6) enters at 65 on an organ: Dmaj9#11 / Ebmaj7#11 on its 8-beat cycle, the split ebbing and flowing but drifting toward D (4+4 ... 7+1) until the last cycle before the jet is 8+0 - D alone, the Eb's pull gone: the tide resolves on the jet. E7 'the jet' (t7) fires from 81 on a brass synth - D3 A3 E4 B4 F#5 C#6 G#6 on 2 2 2 1 1 1 2 sixteenths, 11, prime - crescendo, phased so a column STARTS on beat 384; at bar 97 the column fires and HOLDS on a supersaw (explicit overlapping notes), the whole Lydian collection as one chord under the choir's E8, and again at the jet's return (129); after the jet the column is re-barred into the lock every 4 bars. Adding them alone LOST 2.4 points (structure 88 -> 71: the stretto and the jet merged into one 108-bar block, length_cv 1.4), so the stretto got shape: a FALSE CALM at 57-64 (E2, the pedal and E1 step out; E3's pad and E5's marimba alone) before drums, tide and pedal arrive together at 65, and a VACUUM in the bar before the jet (only the riser and E7's columns). Sections 9 -> 10, length_cv 1.11 -> 0.92, structure and recurrence 100. Seeds 0/11: HEAD 87.48 / 87.83 -> v2 96.99 / 97.28 (+9.5 / +9.4); spectrum 76-79, flow 88-89. Levels -11.1 LUFS, TP -1.29. The detector still does not split AT the jet (the 1-bar vacuum is under its minimum length): the arrival's force is NOT verified by ear.

Rebalanced so every element sounds in its own register: E2 moved to a modal glock, E6 -5 dB, lights -2; E1 +4, E3 +2, E5 +1, E7 +7 (its re-barred columns after the jet vel 72 -> 96), the jet column +7, snare +10, hats +5, crash +4, bass +2. And chirper-one's overshoot: the tide's last two cycles before the jet are 7+1 then 8+0 - the last Eb a single beat, a final tug before it lets go. note: v5 (ROUND TYPE section, EXTENDED to the whole track per Harry 00:30 - 'quite ugly chaos... missing aesthetics and catchiness/hook... atonal, very tough listening... play with time and texture' - and the album direction 'tone is home'): THE TONAL REWORK. t8's stretto was built to rub (E2's F, E3's Eb, E5's G# against the D pedal, E6's semitone tide) and its jet was a HELD 7-NOTE STACK OF FIFTHS (D A E B F# C# G#: a cluster); the v4 horizon transposed echoes by semitones against a sliding held D (a detuned cloud). Every TIME idea kept (phasing to one downbeat, the tide's moving split, the entries, the slowing horizon); every clash dropped: the stretto is consonant D MINOR - E3 as chirper-two's v2 (D | Bb | C, i - VI - VII), E5's G# -> G, E6's tide Dm9 against Bbmaj9, E7's column open fifths (D A E A D E A), E4 minor (Dm9 Bbmaj7 Am7 Dsus2); the jet turns D MAJOR: E7 lands held as D(add9) - its F# the arrival of E8's third - and E4 cleanly major (D9 Bbmaj9 Am7 Dsus2; E2 keeps F natural over the Bb bars); the choir's G#s are G. THE HOOK: after the jet E1 is stated plainly, augmented to two bars, every two bars, on its own track (the chip lead that carried E1 through the stretto) at -3.2 dB vs the mix (presence, K-weighted). Horizon: echoes at pitch (slower, quieter, darker), and the pitch sink waits for bar 161 when only the held light and the 'ah' remain, sinking together. Crash +12 dB (eco's BURIED flag: -29 -> -18). Pitch classes: stretto C D E F G A Bb only; jet D major plus the borrowed Bbmaj9; no Eb/G#/C# anywhere. Seeds 0/11 under the new 7-cut rule: HEAD 98.42 / 98.51 -> v5 96.24 / 96.03 (-2.2 / -2.5: recurrence 97 -> 80-83) - KEPT per Harry's direction (a score may dip; ears over metrics).
